research: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/speech-generation: prebuilt voice characters (Kore firm, Leda youthful, Gacrux mature, Sulafat warm, Achernar soft, Erinome clear, Vindemiatrix gentle, Pulcherrima forward); long director's-note blocks are the main cause of voice drift, so keep style short; punctuation, ellipses and dashes carry hesitation and cut-offs; capitals for emphasis.
https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/is-there-an-update-to-gemini-tts-gemini-went-british/87084: name the accent as a specific place (e.g. a town) rather than a broad 'British accent'.
https://livekit.com/blog/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-prompting-guide: use short labels and never quote transcript words in the note, or the engine may read the note aloud.
https://dev.to/googleai/how-to-prompt-gemini-31s-new-text-to-speech-model-24bb: Google's 3.1 prompting post uses Accent / Style / Pace style notes with a plain place name for accent.
https://replicate.com/google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts/readme: confirms the same 30 voice names and one-word characters carry over to 3.1 Flash TTS.

options.idea: Mid-fifties Yorkshire veteran, twenty-five years on the road; Gacrux is the 'mature' voice, lower and lived-in, fits a senior medic.
options.note:
Accent: Leeds, working class, ordinary and light, nothing put on.
Style: Veteran paramedic in her fifties, shouting at the driver over a siren, then quiet to the dying old man beside her, steady, almost kind.
Pace: Fast and hard, then slow and soft.

options.idea: Early-forties South London medic, clipped and in command; Kore is the 'firm' voice, a woman used to being obeyed.
options.note:
Accent: South London, working class, everyday and natural, not exaggerated.
Style: Forty-year-old paramedic, sharp and furious with the driver, angry at the traffic not him, then barely above a breath to her patient.
Pace: Quick and clipped, then hushed.

options.idea: Mid-thirties Glaswegian, warm by nature and frightened under the swearing; Sulafat is the 'warm' voice, so the quiet last line can carry tenderness.
options.note:
Accent: Glasgow, working class, soft and everyday, not stagey.
Style: Thirty-five-year-old paramedic, scared and swearing because she is scared, yelling forward to the driver, then gently to the old man as he slips away.
Pace: Breathless and urgent, then slow.

notes: Script punctuation should carry the cut-off on the last word (an em dash). No source compared these voices specifically for British accents, so voice fit is by Google's one-word character labels, not by listening (unverified).
